headline: Growth accelerates as buybacks compress the balance sheet
summary_short: Insulet's Q1 2026 revenue rose 33.9% y/y to $761.7 million and diluted EPS more than doubled to $1.30, while gross margin slipped 240bps to 69.5% on inventory-reserve and warranty costs tied to a voluntary Omnipod 5 device correction; the quarter also saw $300 million of accelerated share repurchases.
summary_long: Q1 2026 revenue grew 33.9% y/y to $761.7M (U.S. +28.3% to $515.6M, Int'l +59.4% to $242.9M) on customer growth and higher price. Gross margin fell 240bps to 69.5% on inventory reserves from a Pod-configuration transition and warranty costs from a March 2026 device correction (~$30M total, most in 2026). Operating income rose 37.8% to $122.2M; Adjusted EBITDA rose 35.7% to $181.7M despite R&D +50.6% and SG&A +21.7%. Net income more than doubled to $91.1M ($1.30 diluted EPS) on a lower 19.4% tax rate. Free cash flow +73.4% to $89.5M. A $300M buyback cut cash to $480.4M (-32.9% q/q) and equity to $1,302.6M (-14.0% q/q). Guidance: FY2026 net interest expense ~$40M; no revenue/EPS range in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed: growth driven by a growing Omnipod 5 customer base and higher pricing, with profitability gains despite a one-time gross-margin hit from a voluntary device correction and continued R&D/SG&A investment.
Company-disclosed: constant-currency growth of 30.1% was primarily driven by higher sales volume from a growing customer base, and to a lesser extent higher price.

Company-disclosed: driven by higher inventory excess/obsolescence reserves during the Pod-configuration transition and higher warranty costs from the March 2026 voluntary device correction, partly offset by manufacturing efficiencies and higher ASP.
Company-disclosed: continued investment in Omnipod pipeline products, including a closed-loop AID system for type 2 diabetes and next-generation Omnipod 6.
Company-disclosed: primarily headcount additions in commercial and customer-experience teams to support market-share gains and retention, plus international market-development investment.
Derived-arithmetic: 33.9% revenue growth outpaced combined R&D/SG&A growth in dollar terms, lifting operating income despite the 240bp gross-margin compression.
Company-disclosed: operating-income growth plus a lower 19.4% effective tax rate (vs 26.4% prior year), driven by R&D credits and no repeat of the prior-year convertible-debt extinguishment charge.
Company-disclosed: primarily attributable to net income growth, partially offset by a $32.3M working-capital outflow tied to the annual cash-bonus payout.
Company-disclosed: higher operating income (adjusted for D&A and stock comp) and a smaller working-capital outflow, partially offset by higher capital expenditures.
Company-disclosed: the $300 million accelerated share repurchase agreement, completed during the quarter, was the primary use of cash.
Derived-arithmetic: the $300M ASR buyback reduced paid-in capital/treasury balances by more than net income added, producing the q/q equity decline.
